h: The artists' town, and the stars above it
p: Kirkcudbright has a long and much-loved reputation as an artists' town, and two places help tell that story brilliantly. Broughton House on the High Street was home to the painter E. A. Hornel, one of the Glasgow Boys, and is cared for by the National Trust for Scotland. Its Japanese-inspired garden runs down towards the river and is a real hidden gem. Kirkcudbright Galleries, in the old town hall, show work by the many artists who've been drawn to the town over the years.

The Stewartry Museum is another good stop, packed with local history, from wildlife to everyday life in old Galloway. All of them are close together, so you can walk between them with a coffee break or two.

To follow up a planetarium show with the real thing, head into the Galloway Forest Park. It became the UK's first Dark Sky Park in 2009, and on a clear, moonless night the sky above it is crammed with stars. A few tips: give your eyes time to adjust, bring a red torch, and wear far more layers than seems sensible, as rural Scottish nights get cold fast even outside winter.
The coast around Kirkcudbright is wonderful for walking and rock-pooling by day, so you can easily turn a planetarium trip into a long weekend in this quiet, beautiful corner of the south-west.
